it-2005-cs-70.approach: Test each candidate X → Y by computing the attribute closure X⁺ under the given FDs; X → Y is implied exactly when Y ⊆ X⁺.

steps.title: Closures of the left sides
steps.body:
- $\{C,D\}^+$: $CD\to E$ gives $E$, $E\to A$ gives $A$, $A\to B$ gives $B$ ⇒ $\{A,B,C,D,E\}$.
- $\{B,D\}^+$: $B\to D$ adds nothing new; no FD has a left side inside $\{B,D\}$ other than $B$ ⇒ $\{B,D\}$.
- $\{B,C\}^+$: $B\to D$ gives $D$, then $CD\to E$, $E\to A$ ⇒ $\{A,B,C,D,E\}$.
- $\{A,C\}^+$: $A\to B$, $B\to D$, $CD\to E$ ⇒ $\{A,B,C,D,E\}$.

steps.title: Check each right side
steps.body: $AC\subseteq CD^+$, $CD\subseteq BC^+$, $BC\subseteq AC^+$ — all implied. But $C\notin\{B,D\}^+$, so $BD\to CD$ is **not** implied.

optionAnalysis.reason: $CD^+$ contains $A$ and $C$, so $CD\to AC$ is implied.
$BD^+=\{B,D\}$ lacks $C$, so $BD\to CD$ is not implied — this is the answer.
$BC^+$ is every attribute, so $BC\to CD$ is implied.
$A\to B$ gives $AC\to BC$ by augmentation.

it-2005-cs-70.shortcut: Only B and D can come from {B, D}; no FD starts from B or D alone except B → D, so C is unreachable.
pitfalls: Forgetting to chain FDs (e.g. CD → E → A → B) when computing a closure.
it-2005-cs-70.verification: Recomputed all four closures; only {B,D}⁺ misses an attribute on the right side.

it-2005-cs-71.approach: For CSMA/CD a sender must still be transmitting when a collision from the far end returns, so frame transmission time ≥ round-trip propagation time.

steps.title: Propagation delay

steps.body: $L_{\min}=2T_p\times B=2\times5\times10^{-6}\times10^9=10^4$ bits $=10000$ bits.

Right number but wrong unit: 10000 bytes is 80000 bits.

steps.body: $\text{MaxWindow}=\min(4\text{ KB},6\text{ KB})=4\text{ KB}=4096$ bytes.

it-2005-cs-74.approach: Total probability: condition on which link is taken; the packet survives a link only if all L bits are error-free.

steps.body: Bits are independent, so $P(\text{no error}\mid L1)=(1-b_1)^L$ and $P(\text{no error}\mid L2)=(1-b_2)^L$.

Multiplying $p_1p_2$ treats taking both links as one event; $(b_1+b_2)^L$ has no meaning here.

it-2005-cs-81-1.approach: Under CAV every track holds the same data as the innermost track; under CLV bit density is constant, so capacity grows in proportion to circumference (i.e. to radius).

steps.title: Track radii
steps.body: Radii 0.5, 1.0, …, 4.0 cm (8 equidistant tracks). Track $k$ has radius $0.5k$ cm, i.e. $k$ times the inner radius.

steps.title: CLV
steps.body: Capacity of track $k$ $=10k$ MB ⇒ total $=10(1+2+\dots+8)=10\times36=360$ MB.

steps.title: CAV
steps.body: Every track $=10$ MB ⇒ total $=8\times10=80$ MB.

optionAnalysis.reason: Swaps the two cases; 80 MB is the CAV total, and 2040 MB matches neither model.
2040 MB does not correspond to any proportional model.
Swaps CLV and CAV.
CLV 360 MB, CAV 80 MB — correct.

pitfalls: Swapping the meanings: CAV keeps sectors per track constant, so outer tracks waste density.
it-2005-cs-81-1.verification: Outer/inner circumference ratio = 8, so the outer CLV track holds 80 MB; the sum 10 + 20 + … + 80 = 360.

it-2005-cs-81-2.approach: Time = seek (inner → outer track) + rotational wait until sector 4 starts + transfer of the sectors holding 1 MB; the platter keeps rotating during the seek.
it-2005-cs-81-2.given:
| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Rotation | 6000 RPM ⇒ 10 ms/rev |
| Sectors/track | 20 ⇒ 0.5 ms each |
| Data/sector (CAV) | 10 MB / 20 = 0.5 MB |
| Seek distance | 4 − 0.5 = 3.5 cm |

steps.title: Seek
steps.body: $\dfrac{0.035\text{ m}}{10\text{ m/s}}=3.5$ ms.

steps.title: Where the head is after the seek
steps.body: During 3.5 ms the disk turns $3.5/0.5=7$ sectors: from the end of sector 5 to the end of sector 12.

steps.title: Rotational wait
steps.body: Sector 4 starts at the end of sector 3. From the end of sector 12: sectors 13–20 (8) and 1–3 (3) = 11 sectors $=11\times0.5=5.5$ ms.

steps.title: Transfer and total
steps.body: 1 MB = 2 sectors = 1 ms. Total $=3.5+5.5+1=10$ ms.

optionAnalysis.reason: 13.5 ms adds a further wait of 3.5 ms (seek not overlapped with rotation).
9.5 ms is one sector short (sector off-by-one).
20 ms is two full rotations, far more than needed.

pitfalls: Forgetting that the platter rotates during the seek.
Using CLV capacities: the drive here is CAV, so every sector holds 0.5 MB.
it-2005-cs-81-2.verification: Elapsed 10 ms is exactly one revolution: the head ends at the end of sector 5 again, which is the end of the second sector read (4, 5). Consistent.

it-2005-cs-83-1.approach: Only the rule E → E + E can cause ambiguity, because * always comes with its own parentheses. A string is ambiguous only if it has two or more + at the same parenthesis level.

steps.body: $(E*E)$ is fully bracketed, so it parses one way. $E+E$ with operands $x_1+x_2+x_3$ can group as $(x_1+x_2)+x_3$ or $x_1+(x_2+x_3)$.

One + whose right operand is a fully bracketed product — unique parse.

it-2005-cs-84-1.approach: The first loop is candidate elimination: compare candidate i with each later j. If i → j is absent, j cannot be the sink, so keep i; if i → j exists, i cannot be the sink, so make j the candidate.

steps.title: E1: when to skip j
steps.body: Keep scanning while $A[i][j]=0$: $j$ lacks the edge $i\to j$, so $j$ is not a sink. Hence E1 = \`!A[i][j]\`.

steps.title: E2: when the loop stops
steps.body: It stops at the first $j$ with $A[i][j]=1$; then $i$ has an outgoing edge and cannot be the sink, so the new candidate is $j$: E2 = \`i = j\`.

steps.title: Why it ends with the only candidate
steps.body: Every vertex skipped or abandoned is eliminated, so after one pass i is the only possible sink, checked in O(n) by the second loop.

optionAnalysis.reason: With E1 = A[i][j], j is skipped exactly when i has an edge to it — the opposite of the elimination rule.
i = j + 1 skips vertex j, which may well be the sink.
Skip non-neighbours, jump to the first out-neighbour — correct.
Both the condition and the update are wrong.

pitfalls: Advancing to j + 1 and losing the only remaining candidate.
it-2005-cs-84-1.verification: For a 3-vertex graph where 2 is the sink: i=0, A[0][1]=0 so skip 1, A[0][2]=1 so i=2; j=3 ends the loop with i=2.

it-2005-cs-84-2.approach: Candidate i is a sink iff for every j ≠ i: A[i][j] = 0 and A[j][i] = 1. flag must be cleared when either condition fails.

steps.title: Sink condition
steps.body: For all $j\ne i$: $\lnot A[i][j]\land A[j][i]$.

steps.title: Negate for flag = 0
steps.body: $\lnot(\lnot A[i][j]\land A[j][i])=A[i][j]\lor\lnot A[j][i]$ ⇒ E3 = \`(A[i][j] || !A[j][i])\`.

Also true for a correct sink (A[j][i] = 1), so it would reject every sink.
Clears flag exactly when the sink property fails for some j — correct.
